topic: Offtake after Mystic Generating Station retirement (2024)
wiki_text: Everett's original captive offtaker, the 1.4 GW Mystic Generating Station, retired on 31 May 2024. Rather than close Everett alongside Mystic (its founding rationale), Constellation kept the terminal operating; National Grid and other New England utilities pursued ~6-year peak-demand gas supply contracts that are expected to keep Everett open through roughly winter 2029-30 as a regional reliability/peak-shaving safeguard. All of New England's LNG imports (~13.3 Bcf in the prior year) flowed through Everett.

topic: 2025 DRBC permit extension and litigation; feedgas-by-rail collapse
wiki_text: In 2025 New Fortress affiliate Delaware River Partners sought to extend its DRBC dock-construction permit; in September 2025 the Delaware River Basin Commission granted a second five-year extension, which the Delaware Riverkeeper Network challenged in a November 2025 suit in the U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey. The project's original feedgas plan — LNG railed/trucked from the Wyalusing liquefaction plant in PA — collapsed when Wyalusing was abandoned as an LNG site (repurposed to a gas-fired data-center power plant); sponsors told FERC in 2024 the export proposal remained active via LNG-by-truck. The project remains proposed (pre-FID) with >$100M sunk costs.

topic: 2025 MARAD license amendment, suspension extended to 2027
wiki_text: On 19 August 2025 MARAD published an amendment to the Neptune LNG deepwater-port license (USCG-2005-22611) extending the temporary suspension of port operations through 31 December 2027, following Neptune's 12 December 2024 request. Neptune stated the continued suspension is necessary while it evaluates decommissioning. Any restart petition must be filed at least six months in advance with all federal/state approvals. The port (operated by Hoegh Evi / Mitsui O.S.K. Lines, ~22 mi NE of Boston) remains mothballed.
